#### 1. T-cell lymphopenia, infantile, with or without nail dystrophy, autosomal dominant  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.786)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:12765)

Loss-of-function mutations in FOXN1 disrupt thymic epithelial cell development and function, leading to severe T-cell lymphopenia and absent thymus. In some cases, this also manifests as nail dystrophy.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in FOXN1 that segregate with a gain-of-function mechanism in either disease would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs149619861)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in FOXN1 allows for the development of targeted therapies for both Nezelof syndrome and infantile T-cell lymphopenia, potentially focusing on thymic regeneration or T-cell reconstitution strategies.
